title: Door lock control experiment (15 subjects, 4 classes, 31 EEG ch)
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 15 healthy subjects performing a P300-based brain-computer interface task for door lock control. The experiment employed a visual oddball paradigm with 31-channel EEG acquisition at 500 Hz, yielding target and non-target event classifications across 50 training and 30 testing trials per subject. The data supports the development and evaluation of P300-based BCI systems for home appliance control applications.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a 31-channel actiCHamp system (Brain Products) at 500 Hz sampling rate with linked mastoid reference and active sensors. The standard 10-20 montage was employed. Subjects performed a visual oddball task with flash stimuli presented on an LCD display at 750 ms stimulus onset asynchrony. Each session included 50 training and 30 testing blocks per subject.
